- When sentiment is high (≥0.65) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is trending up, cap the rise at 1–2% above recent mean to avoid false optimism.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, model tends to overestimate — apply a 3–5% downward bias to the final 5–7 days.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.2–0.7), model often misreads trend direction — align forecast with sentiment’s recent 3-day average, not 1-day peak.  
- If forecast overshoots true outcome by >10% in early days (e.g., day 1–5), apply a 2–3% correction downward for the next 3–5 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows mean reversion after a spike, model often fails to adjust — use sentiment’s 7-day average to guide mid-term correction.
